prompt.content: You narrate one moment of a quiet, literary horror story in second person, present tense. Write two or three short sentences with one concrete physical detail (the ink, your hands, the light, a sound). Use only the facts given. Never explain what is happening, and never mention timelines.

Where you are: your apartment, 6C. With you: no one. The power is out; the only light is the storm's.
What changed: the photo of my sister (in your hand) now has "8209" written on it. It was not there a moment ago.
Let the reader sense, without saying it outright, that the handwriting is Mara's.
Write the moment you notice it, in normal sentences. Name the photo of my sister in your first sentence. Quote the writing exactly as "8209". Apart from the writing itself, use no numbers and no words in ALL CAPS.

D.narration: You hold the photo of my sister. Fresh ink in your own handwriting reads "DO NOT LOOK BEHIND YOU". Lightning flashes across the roof.

prompt.content: You narrate one moment of a quiet, literary horror story in second person, present tense. Write two or three short sentences with one concrete physical detail (the ink, your hands, the light, a sound). Use only the facts given. Never explain what is happening, and never mention timelines.

Where you are: the roof. With you: no one. The power is out; the only light is the storm's.
What changed: the photo of my sister (in your hand) now has "DO NOT LOOK BEHIND YOU" written on it. It was not there a moment ago.
Let the reader sense, without saying it outright, that the handwriting is your own, but you never wrote it.
Write the moment you notice it, in normal sentences. Name the photo of my sister in your first sentence. Quote the writing exactly as "DO NOT LOOK BEHIND YOU". Apart from the writing itself, use no numbers and no words in ALL CAPS.

ending.text:
You choose this night. Only this one.

The writing fades: "8209" then "DO NOT LOOK BEHIND YOU" from the photo of my sister, like breath off a mirror, and then there is nothing left to read.

Far below, a metal door closes, gently, and does not open again.

At 12:30 the power comes back all at once, every light in the building, and the fridge begins to hum as if nothing happened. Nothing did.

You will never know what happened in the night you didn't choose. You will think about it on stairs for the rest of your life.
